_comment: llama-multimodel-mcp profiles. Copy to ~/.llama-mm/profiles.json (or point config.profiles_file at it). The top-level 'default' profile is used whenever a tool call omits profile_id — the example defaults to LM Studio's standard port 1234, so if LM Studio is running with a model loaded, chat/usage_stats work zero-config. provider: 'llama-server' = full lifecycle (start/stop/bench/telemetry, needs model paths); 'openai-compatible' = inference + stats against a running server (LM Studio :1234, Ollama :11434/v1, vLLM, llama-swap). tier drives workflow routing: 'quality' = high-quality executor, 'bulk' = fast/rough executor. llama-server profiles also accept: 'device' (GPU pool name; VRAM budgets are checked per pool via config.vram_budget_by_device and switch_profile only restarts instances in the same pool), 'vram_gb' (override weight_gb for budget accounting, e.g. CPU-offload tiers), 'host' (llama-server on another machine — start/stop/switch refuse, chat/complete/bench go over HTTP).

lmstudio.description: Zero-config default: LM Studio (or Ollama /v1, vLLM, llama-swap). model_id null = use whatever the server has loaded; set it to route a specific model.

qwen3.8-27b.description: Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen3.6-27B works too). High-quality coding executor — tune ctx/args to your VRAM.

qwen3.6-35b-a3b.description: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE. Fast/rough executor for mechanical batch work.

qwen3.5-9b.description: Qwen3.5-9B utility profile (quick chat / OCR fallback). No tier = not part of quality/bulk workflow routing; use it explicitly.

remote-workstation-27b.description: llama-server running on another machine: chat/complete/bench go over HTTP; start/stop/switch are refused locally. Start it on the remote box yourself (or via its own llama-mm).
